turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Come through. Your partner's happy to wait outside until you're ready, he said.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, leave him, he's glued to his phone. I'm a bit all over the shop, sorry. We've been up since six because the dog was barking at the bin truck.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): All good. I'll just do a blood pressure and pulse before the doctor. You're not feeling faint sitting there?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Not faint, no. It's this spotting and the cramps that got me in.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Blood pressure is one eighteen over seventy-four, pulse eighty-six. I'll grab the doctor.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this thing's decided to update itself. Right. What's brought you in?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): So I'm pregnant, and I've been spotting. Brown, not heaps. And crampy, low in my belly, like a period. I reckon I'm about eight or ten weeks but I honestly don't know.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hang on, it just pinged. Say again how many weeks?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): About eight to ten? The last period was around Diwali, or after. I can't pin the day. We had family over, there was so much food, my auntie made that carrot halwa, I ate way too much, totally off topic, sorry.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's alright. When did the spotting start?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, a few days. Maybe since the weekend, or a bit before that. I keep losing track of which morning I first saw it.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the cramps, did they start then too?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, same sort of time. They come and go, not all day. Worse when I'm on my feet. I do reception at a physio in Parramatta, so I'm up and down all arvo, and the M4 this morning was a car park.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. Any heavy bleeding, clots, soaking through a pad?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. It's just a bit of brown when I wipe.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is the pain more on one side?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose, sometimes, not really. It sort of moves around.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any shoulder pain, or dizziness?

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No shoulder pain. I went a bit woozy in the shower yesterday but it passed, I just stood up too quick. My sister's like that, she's anaemic, forever telling me to eat spinach.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): So the wooziness isn't hanging around?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No, gone.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nausea? Vomiting?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. Not vomiting. The neighbour's curry last night was a bit much but I still ate, we had leftovers for tea.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pain or burning when you pass urine?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I don't think so. I haven't actually checked with a thermometer.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): What are you taking?

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Folic acid. Um, the one milligram— no, wait, GP put me on five milligrams, once a day, because we were trying. And Elevit, the pregnancy one, most mornings. I skipped a couple when I felt off, but mostly I take it.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the screen jumped. Folate dose again?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Five milligrams, once a day.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines or anything else?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that I know of. I had penicillin as a kid for tonsillitis and I was fine.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any operations?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No, never. Oh, and I've got asthma, had it since I was a teenager, but it's quiet, I haven't touched the puffer in months.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Asthma, quiet, noted. Do you smoke?

[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. And I stopped drinking when the test turned positive. We live together, me and my partner, over in Westmead. He's still outside, poor thing, he hates waiting rooms, reckons the magazines are from 2004.
[SEG0038] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sorry to butt in. He's asked if he can come in now. And ultrasound have a slot at two today if you want it.

[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah send him in, he can just sit. I'm properly anxious about this, hey. I barely slept last night, just going over worst cases. He's not going to talk, he goes quiet at the doctor.

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's understandable. I'm not calling this a miscarriage. It might be a threatened miscarriage, or it might just be benign spotting this early. With the dates all over the place we need a look.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. The home test was positive, two lines, about three weeks ago I think, or maybe a bit less, I didn't write it down.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. We'll do a pelvic ultrasound today, that two o'clock slot, and bloods today as well: a pregnancy hormone level, a full blood count, and your blood group.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I have to keep taking the Elevit and the folate?

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, keep both going, same as you are. No new tablets from me today. Take it easy, no heavy lifting this week, and if you're standing all day at work see if you can sit more.

[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): I can ask my boss. She's pretty good. We had a staff morning tea yesterday, someone brought lamingtons, I had two, which is probably not the issue but I feel guilty about everything now.

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Lamingtons won't have done this. If the bleeding gets heavy, you soak a pad within an hour, the pain gets severe, or you feel faint, come straight to emergency, don't wait for me.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Straight to emergency. Okay. And if it's just this same spotting?
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then I still want you back here in a week with the results, even if it settles. Don't skip that one.
[SEG0049] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I'll book the ultrasound for two and put the blood forms through to pathology downstairs so you can go after this.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. If my partner looks pale it's just him, not me. He nearly fainted at his own blood test last year, dramatic.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll keep an eye on you, not him. Any questions before I let you go?
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): I think that's it. I'll try not to google myself into a state before two.
